# package implicit

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-ethernetip/implicit"
```

Package implicit is EtherNet/IP implicit (I/O) messaging: the codec of Class 0 and Class 1 datagrams, a UDP [Endpoint](#type-endpoint) that receives them on port 2222 and dispatches them by connection ID, and the [Connection](#type-connection) that produces and consumes the data of one connection at its requested packet intervals, with sequence handling, run/idle and the inactivity watchdog.

The scanner package (originator) and the server package (target) build their I/O connections on it; Forward\_Open itself is theirs.

## Constants

```go
const RunBit uint32 = 1
```

RunBit is the run bit of the 32-bit run/idle header.

## Types

### type Config

```go
type Config struct {
	// Class is the transport class, 0 or 1.
	Class uint8

	// ProducedID is the connection ID of the datagrams this end sends;
	// zero when it sends none.
	ProducedID uint32
	// Destination is where the datagrams are sent: the peer's address and
	// I/O port, or a multicast group.
	Destination netip.AddrPort
	// ProduceRPI is the interval of production; required when ProducedID
	// is set.
	ProduceRPI time.Duration
	// ProduceFormat and ProduceSize are the real-time format and the size
	// of the application data produced (without sequence count and
	// header).
	ProduceFormat Format
	ProduceSize   int
	// Produce returns the data to send and whether to send run (true) or
	// idle; it is called at every production. The slice is copied. A nil
	// Produce sends ProduceSize zero octets, run.
	Produce func() (data []byte, run bool)

	// ConsumedID is the connection ID of the datagrams this end receives;
	// zero when it receives none.
	ConsumedID uint32
	// Timeout is the inactivity timeout of consumption: without a valid
	// datagram for this long the connection times out. Zero disables it.
	Timeout time.Duration
	// FirstTimeout, when set, replaces Timeout until the first datagram
	// (some targets need longer to start producing).
	FirstTimeout time.Duration
	// ConsumeFormat and ConsumeSize are the format and the size of the
	// application data consumed; with ConsumeVariable the size is a
	// maximum.
	ConsumeFormat   Format
	ConsumeSize     int
	ConsumeVariable bool
	// Source, when valid, is the only address consumed datagrams are
	// accepted from (the port is not checked: originators send from any
	// port).
	Source netip.Addr
	// Group, when valid, is a multicast group to join for consumption,
	// on interface Interface (nil for the system's choice).
	Group     netip.Addr
	Interface *net.Interface
	// OnData is called with the data of each consumed datagram that
	// carries new data (a newer Class 1 sequence count; every datagram for
	// Class 0), and whether it says run. It runs on the endpoint's
	// receiving goroutine: it must not block. data is only valid during
	// the call.
	OnData func(data []byte, run bool)
	// OnTimeout is called once when consumption times out; the connection
	// stops producing and is closed.
	OnTimeout func()
}
```

Config describes one I/O connection as seen from one end. "Produce" is the direction this end sends, "consume" the one it receives: for an originator O->T and T->O, for a target the reverse.

### type Connection

```go
type Connection struct {

	// a datagram was consumed: reset the watchdog
	// produce now

	// last produced
	// last produced
	// last produced data
	// last produced run/idle
	// last consumed
	// last consumed
	// a datagram was consumed

}
```

Connection is one open I/O connection on an [Endpoint](#type-endpoint).

#### func (Connection) Close

```go
func (c *Connection) Close()
```

Close stops the connection: production ends and consumed datagrams are no longer accepted. OnTimeout is not called. Close is idempotent.

#### func (Connection) Done

```go
func (c *Connection) Done() <-chan struct{}
```

Done is closed when the connection is closed or has timed out.


Stats returns the connection's counters.

#### func (Connection) TimedOut

```go
func (c *Connection) TimedOut() bool
```

TimedOut reports whether the connection ended by timeout.

#### func (Connection) Trigger

```go
func (c *Connection) Trigger()
```

Trigger produces a datagram now, in addition to the cyclic ones: a change of state or an application trigger.

### type Endpoint

```go
type Endpoint struct {

	// consumers by consumed connection ID
	// every open connection, producers too
	// multicast memberships, counted
	// the interface address each group was joined on
	// the default multicast interface address

	// faults, when set (by the package's chaos tests), decides the fate of
	// each datagram sent: it returns the datagrams to send now, which may
	// be none (dropped), the datagram twice (duplicated) or older ones
	// (reordered). It is called with the endpoint's send lock held.

}
```

Endpoint is a UDP socket of I/O messages: it receives datagrams and hands each to the [Connection](#type-connection) whose consumed connection ID it carries, and sends the datagrams of its connections. Several connections share one endpoint. An Endpoint is safe for concurrent use.

#### func WithMulticastInterface

```go
func WithMulticastInterface(ifi *net.Interface) EndpointOption
```

WithMulticastInterface sets the interface the endpoint sends multicast from and joins groups on, when a connection does not name one (Config.Interface). By default an endpoint bound to one address uses that address's interface, and one bound to the wildcard address leaves the choice to the system (the interface of the default route). Note that an endpoint bound to a unicast address does not receive multicast on most systems: a consuming endpoint binds the wildcard address.

### type Format

```go
type Format uint8
```

Format is the real-time format of one direction of a connection: what precedes the application data.

```go
const (
	// FormatModeless carries the data alone; the usual T->O format.
	FormatModeless Format = 0
	// FormatZeroLength carries no data: a packet means run, its absence
	// idle.
	FormatZeroLength Format = 1
	// FormatHeartbeat carries no data: the packets only keep the
	// connection alive (input-only and listen-only connections).
	FormatHeartbeat Format = 2
	// FormatHeader32 prefixes the data with the 32-bit run/idle header; the
	// usual O->T format.
	FormatHeader32 Format = 3
)
```

Real-time formats.

#### func (Format) Overhead

```go
func (f Format) Overhead(class uint8) int
```

Overhead returns the octets a Class 1 (class 1) or Class 0 (class 0) connection adds to the application data in this format: the 16-bit sequence count (Class 1) and the 32-bit header (FormatHeader32). The connection size of a Forward\_Open is the data size plus Overhead.

#### func (Format) String

```go
func (f Format) String() string
```

String returns "modeless", "zero-length", "heartbeat" or "header32".

```go
	ConnID uint32

}
```

#### func Decode

```go
func Decode(b []byte) (Message, error)
```

Decode decodes a datagram. Items other than the sequenced address and the connected data (Sockaddr Info items) are ignored. The payload aliases b.

```go
func (m Message) Encode() ([]byte, error)
```

Encode returns the datagram: a common packet format of a sequenced address item and a connected data item.
